text:
DeployBot: ALERT: canary deployment v3.2.1 at 25% traffic — error-rate spike to 6.8% (p95 latency +40%). Suggested action: REVIEW / possible rollback. runbook: https://rwd.infra/runbooks/canary-failures

sanjay: seen this. metrics look correlated with a new tokenization change in the tokenizer service.

melissa: rolling at 25% only. Are errors user-facing or just internal 5xxs?

kevin: stack traces show 500s from model-proxy timeouts, probably kvcache eviction spike after the change.

ops-oncall: if it's model-proxy timeouts at canary we should either revert canary or pin traffic back and execute manual rollback. Auto-rollback threshold is 5% but that would kick a full revert — want to confirm impact first.

pm-oliver: FYI some high-usage customers in EU on dedicated may be affected if this expands. Recommend comms ready regardless.

cs-liz: please ping me if we plan a rollback — I'll prepare customer messages and support playbook.

kevin: proposal: pause promotion, pin canary to 0% by routing, then do a controlled manual rollback of model-serving replica set to v3.2.0 in canary pool. After validation promote again. That avoids full auto-revert which touches stable. :thinking_face:

melissa: agree with manual rollback. Auto rollback would flip more than we want.

DeployBot: Deploy policy trigger: error-rate >5% for 3 consecutive minutes. Auto-rollback window is enabled between 02:00-22:00 UTC. Current time inside window.

ops-oncall: I'll run the rollback. Steps: 1) run `kubectl -n inference set image deploy/model-serving model-serving=registry.redwood/v3.2.0 --record` 2) scale down any v3.2.1 pods: `kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/model-serving --to-revision=...` 3) pin traffic in router: `rwdctl route set canary --weight 0` 4) monitor canary-metrics dashboard and logs for 10m.

ops-oncall: quick command snippet:
```
# Pin canary to 0%
rwdctl route update --env prod --traffic canary=0
# Rollback canary pool
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/model-serving --to-revision=112
```

kevin: add a short hold policy so deploybot won't try to re-promote: `deploybot hold v3.2.1 --reason "manual rollback in progress" --expires 1768547150`

ops-oncall: doing step 1-3 now. I'll post progress.

DeployBot: ACTION: Traffic update accepted by router. canary=0. Actor=ops-oncall.

ops-oncall: executing rollback to rev 112 (v3.2.0). starting rollout...

melissa: heads-up to eng-oncall and perf: watch p50/p95 and kvcache evictions.

kevin: notifying release leads and adding entry to release-notes: "v3.2.1 canary rollback due to proxy timeouts; manual rollback to v3.2.0; follow-up investigation ongoing"

cs-liz: customer comms drafted: short status email and PSAT for impacted accounts. Will queue once rollback validated.

DeployBot: Rollout status: 3/3 updated replicas. health checks passing.

ops-oncall: canary metrics look stable for the last 8 minutes. p95 back to baseline. No new 5xx.

pm-oliver: good. Please keep v3.2.1 blocked from promotion until root cause fixed.

kevin: adding block: `release-control pin v3.2.1 --status blocked --notes "requires fix for kvcache eviction leading to proxy timeouts"`.

ops-oncall: done. Release pinned and auto-promote disabled for v3.2.1.

melissa: great job. postmortem owners? sanjay and kevin volunteer to lead RCA.

sanjay: I'll own RCA and timeline. Will include perf and infra.

cs-liz: I'm sending the customer note now.

kevin: final check: should we run additional smoke tests in staging before allowing a new canary?

melissa: yes. staging + small internal canary with synthetic load. we'll only re-open promotion after sign-off from RCA and perf team.

ops-oncall: closing this thread — rollback complete and customers notified. tagging for follow-up: @sanjay @kevin @melissa @cs-liz. :white_check_mark:
